utterances.text: Can I have a look at it? Because the two are not related, the fact that he had his own artillery and that he could neutralise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We mean Kovacevic, the commander of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I mean him as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any instructions to use his own artillery in the absence of additional support? He didn't have large-calibre cannons, but he had mortars. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Certainly, he knew that as the commander. Why would I need to say it? It is not correlated; it is not in the same context, the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you say it, speaking of mortars?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: The first part of the answer is correct and I still think that is true. But the second time, the second part speaking of the use of pieces, I don't remember that. Why would I have said that? According to regulation, he would have neutralised the sources of fire from which he was being targeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the first sentence on that page of the interview, 205: "I said to him he has his own artillery and let him neutralise those firing positions."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: All right. But I don't remember it. I remember the part about the artillery. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now reading the end of page 206 and the beginning of page 207 of the English version: Question of the investigator: "Q. So the Old Town was being shelled. And if I understood correctly what you said, there was quite a lot of confusion on the front line, and it was difficult to stop the attack.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I noted that later. But at that moment, I couldn't understand why the attack was not being stopped. For a while, I thought they were hesitating and dragging their feet with the withdrawal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you mean by `they'?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Well, Zec and Kovacevic. At 12.00, I was informed that preparations were underway, that the withdrawal was beginning, but only by parts of some company, whereas some parts, according to them, were unable to withdraw, to pull out. And then, leaving for Belgrade, I sent Zec the message that he should complete the withdrawal and prevent further losses to battalion. As required, he may neutralise sources of fire, but not with our artillery. As far as I remember, that was the last thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With what artillery then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Their battalion artillery." Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I must have if that's what's written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jokic, if I understood you well, you said that on the 5th of December you did not have any briefing involving the making of reports, and you didn't attend one. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between July 2002 and September 2003, did you make any preparations in terms of investigation and studying of the case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I was able to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll read to you now a part of your interview given to investigators in September 2003, page number 113 of the English version, of course. You were being questioned by the investigator about what you were doing after the negotiations on the 5th of December. And the question is: "Did you convey that order down the chain to your subordinate units?" "A. I returned to my forward command post in Kupari and advised my command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Then I went to Kumbor. I finished that business, and I returned to Kumbor because I had some problems to solve involving the evacuation of the Pula sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed that the last time, too. Did you issue the order that -- Strugar's order on cease-fire should be passed on down the chain to subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that done? Was it passed on, your order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I personally ordered my commanders at the briefing, and I ordered my chief of staff as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your subordinate commanders report to your chief of staff on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of the commander of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: He wasn't there. He attended briefings only rarely." Is that what you stated, Mr. Jokic, in September 2003?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: If that is what is written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true, what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I don't remember any briefing, any making of reports. I only remember the preparation in my command and the passing on of the information. But it's true if it's written, and no other commander was supposed to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a briefing on the 5th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No. I'm saying there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your interview says that there definitely was one, and at that briefing you informed the commanders and issued an order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: There were no commanders. Not a single commander was there. If the commander of the 3rd Battalion was there, nobody else was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how come that on the 6th of December regarding the ban on the use of artillery, the 130-millimetre cannons, how did you enforce that ban?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Through an order. I ordered Kozaric, the chief of operations, and the chief of staff, Zec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see Zec on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of December when I returned from Belgrade, I also spoke to him on the telephone twice, when he came to Kupari in the morning and before I left for Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him before leaving for Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I think I even saw him then. I'm not sure. But I believe I even saw him. I'm not sure, however. I know that I sent a dispatch that was addressed to Minister Rudolf, and I'm not sure if it had been forwarded because it hadn't been typed. But the contents was dictated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In earlier examination and cross-examination, why didn't you mention it once before?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I wasn't asked. I'm now telling you that I gave the contents of the dispatch to Captain Nemenija Kurdulija to be given to Zec. I don't remember for that time or any other time whether I gave it personally to Zec or I gave it to Kurdulija to pass it on to Zec. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which dispatch are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: The last dispatch around 1400 hours or maybe 1300 hours, something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may remind you, it's not about the time, it's about the dispatch. Is that the one sent to Minister Rudolf mentioning that you have to go to Belgrade and that General Kadijevic had ordered an investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as that dispatch is concerned, you're not sure whether you had given it to Zec or Kurdulija. And who is Kurdulija?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: That is an officer from the sector command. He was at the command in Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I'll now read out to you from the interview of September 2003, page in the English version 160. "Q. So you recommended to General Strugar to remove Jovanovic, and he did that. He replaced him.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had done it at all, or maybe somebody else from his command did. He had only come for five days, and he was supposed to go back to Podgorica anyway." Further below at the end of that page 160 and beginning of page 161 of the English version, the investigator asks: "Q. All right. Maybe we digressed a bit. But tell me, what were the circumstances of Jovanovic's replacement, I mean replacement by you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I replaced him because that Lieutenant Colonel Djurasic brought me a paper stating exactly which mortars were used, which targets were shot at in Dubrovnik, and at what time. He could not conceal it and say, `I don't know who fired.' It was a fact." Mr. Jokic, is that what you stated in September 2003?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your statement true?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: As far as the firing itself is concerned, of course it's true. The same is written in the war diary, in my own notebooks, all the officers of the command know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything that's untrue in what you stated here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: The issue of the replacement, I can't be sure. I wasn't sure then and I'm not sure now how it was actually carried out, whether he was replaced directly through my order, whether it was something that I suggested and he was actually replaced by another operations group. I'm not sure how it replacement was executed, how it was carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But is this second part concerning Lieutenant Colonel Djurasic true?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct. And the entry in the war diary is also correct. We found it in the archives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me about Lieutenant Colonel Djurasic. That paper with all those specifications of targets, ammunition expenditure, et cetera, when did he give it to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: When I returned from Belgrade sometime in the evening or maybe it was already there waiting for me. I think it was at that time. In fact, it's not that I think, it must have been then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you check the data from that paper in the logbook of the operations centre, the forward command post at Kupari?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it in the logbook then. I saw it now when I was preparing my case in the military archives. There were exact indications, exact data, and I know it by heart. 120 millimetres, 42 shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We all know it. But is it in the war diary, in the logbook?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: In the one that I consulted in the military archives, yes, it's there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember when you sent this telegram to Minister Rudolf, the one that you said that you don't know whether you handed it to Zec or to Kurdulija?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I do not remember the time. Of course I cannot remember the time. I just know it was before I went to Belgrade. That I know for sure. That means it could have been between 12.00 and 2.00, because I don't know exactly when I went. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may remind you, in P162 on page 18, on page 18, do you have that diary in front of you of the port authority?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 18, the entry at 11.45.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the port authority at 11.45 received for the of Dubrovnik for Minister Davorin Rudolf from the VPO Boka. Could you please look at it briefly and just tell me whether that's your telegram.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask, I don't see how this necessarily fits into the framework of the rebuttal direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It doesn't have to, as long as it's relevant to the issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Jokic, when answering the questions put to you by my learned friend you said as far as Miroslav Jovanovic was concerned that he was a temporary stand-in for Commander Zdravkovic for the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade and that he was there for two days only, that you personally did not see him and that you do not know him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miroslav Jovanovic, as chief of staff of the 5th Brigade during the months of October and November 1991, did he tour the 3rd Battalion of his brigade, and did he sometimes attend, together with Commander Zdravkovic, the briefings at the forward command post in Kupari?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't know. No, I never met him. I said that. I never met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In December, did Major Zdravkovic ask you for permission to go on leave because of excessive fatigue? He was on the front line, and his birthday was on the 2nd of December and he wanted to spend it with his family.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, no. There was no birthday involved. There was an illness involved. If it was a birthday, he would not have been allowed to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does Zdravkovic propose Jovanovic as a replacement or stand-in for himself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I don't remember that, but I don't think that it was his idea. That is done by the commander of the brigade, and I probably had to ask who his replacement would be. But the commander of the brigade sent a stand-in and said who this would be because I would not let him go. I didn't want to let him go, and I called and I talked to Lieutenant Colonel Kricek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what about the commander of the 9th VPS? Did it send any requests in writing to that effect, to the command of the 5th Brigade in Podgorica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. In relation to that particular matter, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I don't remember. I don't understand, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when Zdravkovic and Jovanovic came to the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, did they receive duty and hand over duty?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think there was any hand over. That kind of thing is not done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. The commander of the 3rd Battalion of the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond 5th Brigade, can he lose -- can he leave his position and not familiarise the person who would be his stand-in with the situation and what the positions were of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: That's a different story. That is not a handover. That is familiarisation with the tactical situation and the command. As for handover of duty, that cannot take place, and that is never done for five days only because the entire battalion has to be lined up and all the leaders of the smaller units. That's a completely different story. So no handover of that kind was ever carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, if I understand you correctly, if I understand what you're saying, when we are talking about transfers and things like that, then it's the way you said it was. However, if a man is coming to take over command of a battalion for two days, three days, five days, never mind, does he have to familiarise himself with the situation on the ground, with the units, with the equipment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: That's what I said, too. However, there is no handover of duty in that sense, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This new commander who comes for a certain period of time, does he have to familiarise himself with the superior command as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: In a normal situation, yes. If he's nearby. But if he's on the other side of Rijeka Dubrovacka and if he's staying for a few days only, then he can also telephone. Why would he come and why would he leave the battalion? Also, it is possible for him to call himself, yes. That's possible. Maybe he did make a telephone call. However, I personally did not see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as support from 130-millimetre cannons is concerned, you said that it was impossible for an officer from the command of the 9th VPS to promise any support, that it could only be you as the commander or your chief of staff. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, even the chief of staff cannot -- or rather, he can do it, but he has to inform me about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that on the 5th of December you did not promise support of 130-millimetre cannons to anyone. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Of course it's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether your chief of staff promised someone 130-millimetre cannons support?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I'm absolutely unaware of any such thing. And I would be greatly surprised if that were the case. But I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I'm just saying, do you know this or do you not know about any such thing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I do not know about any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your chief of staff, did he order a ZIS platoon to be left to the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade until the problem of Srdj is resolved?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. What problem of Srdj? What are you saying? There never was a problem of Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your chief of staff, did he inform you about anything in that sense?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion, did it have a platoon of ZIS cannons on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I think in the area of Vrastica or thereabouts, to the northeast. The ZIS battery while it was there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I'm going to give you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Document D106, Defence Exhibit D106.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, this is a document of the command of the 472nd Motorised Brigade. This is a request for delay of deadline and resubordination of units. Please take a look at the upper right-hand corner, please, the first entry.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you wrote?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature underneath?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read what it says here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: "Chief of staff, view and resolve if possible as requested."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does it say down here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: "Approve not sending ZIS to Zaton, but do not approve taking a ZIS platoon from the 3rd Battalion for as long as the Srdj problem is there. Approve taking of pieces from the warehouse."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the signature?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Zec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zec inform you about why he was leaving the ZIS cannons there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, no, I did not see this. I mean, I saw the document, of course. But until the problem of Srdj is resolved, there never was such a problem. There was the problem of the positions from where provocations were coming, and that was a problem --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this problem of provocations and where they were coming from, is that the Srdj feature?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we were not resolving it in that way, by taking it. There never was a plan to take it either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. You mentioned in relation to Miroslav Jovanovic that you found a report where he was operating and for how long. That's what you referred to a few minutes ago. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when answering the questions put to you by the Prosecutor, you said that you removed him, you had him removed because he was irresponsibly and he was not capable of carrying out his duties?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said you had Jovanovic replaced by telephone?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I'm just saying that as far as the actual replacement is concerned and the course it took, I'm not sure. But my officers, some of my officers say that I personally issued this order over the telephone. But I think that I should have informed the command -- the commander of the 2nd Operative Group, but I'm not sure. I cannot say anything specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you send Colonel Kovacevic to convey that order to him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: That is very possible because he was assistant commander for the land forces. Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown D108. Can we please also prepare Defence Exhibit D113.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we do not have much time. This is a report on the combat operations of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade which was submitted to the command of the 9th VPS by Lieutenant Colonel Miroslav Jovanovic on the 6th of December 1991. What I want to know is whether you saw this report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No. Never. If a commander sees a document, at least he must initial it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from your command have this document concealed from you in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I don't know that this document existed anywhere in my command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Defence Exhibit 113.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, this is Captain Jovica Nesic's report regarding the use of projectiles on the 6th of December 1991 submitted to Battleship Captain Milan Zec. It was written in Kupari on the 8th of December 1991. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, to object. I need to know if I can the numbers of the documents the Chamber indicated were not to be used and whether these may be those documents, that were not to be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a document that was used in our case and has been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The numbers of the three documents that are not to be used, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... At the commencement of today, and a direction was given that those three were not to be put. And we are now putting documents that appear to be of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be allowed to explain, if there's anything that is not clear, the three documents I referred to, Your Honour, are three new documents that have not yet been shown to the Trial Chamber. In the meantime, since the witness's original testimony, these documents have been obtained. But certainly what I said was not in reference to any of the documents that have admitted into evidence. I'm sorry if I was not very clear about it at the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. These are each presently exhibits, and that's consistent with what Mr. Petrovic said this morning, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, briefly, please, tell me if you've ever seen this report.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No. If I'd seen it, it would have been stated right here or written. I've never seen it before. This is the Ploce commander Jovica Nesic's report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone inform you about this, your chief of staff specifically?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No. This report was submitted later on, on the 8th. On the 8th of December, it says here, when there was a request for all the documents of all the subordinate units regarding the attack on Srdj and on the Old Town to be submitted. And when the report was made for General Strugar and for the supreme command. However, I wasn't part of it. I didn't work on these, nor have I ever seen this report. It was never given to me. It was not written on the 6th because the date that is reflected on the document is the 8th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us move on, please. Mr. Jokic, are you fully familiar with the way the telephone communications at the forward command post in Kupari worked, or specifically let me ask you: The Kupari forward command post without any help or intervention from the operations centre in Kumbor, were they able to call Belgrade directly by a military line?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had their own switchboard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about military lines now. Could Belgrade, without the assistance of the switchboard at Kumbor, call directly the forward command post at Kupari?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, they could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military line that ran to Belgrade, was it possible for Belgrade to call you at the forward command post at Kupari or whenever you were around it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could they get through to you in Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, not in Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Because there was no military line available in Cavtat. There was only the civilian telephone line, and they couldn't be put through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a civilian telephone line, do you mean the PTT, the post and telecommunications line?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I have in mind. There was a line to Dubrovnik in the Atlas tourist agency, in their office. There was a cable connection with the town, and that's how I was able to talk to Minister Rudolf on the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, was there any other communications equipment in Cavtat at Captain Kurdulija's command post?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. There was a radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use this radio communication from Cavtat, and if so, who did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I may have been given that piece of equipment to try to get through to Kupari, but I simply can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, did Petre Handzijev have "very good" as his official assessment grade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I know for as long as I was his boss, his assessment was "good," not "very good".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, did Petre Handzijev become the commander of the mixed naval unit of amphibious landing boats which was a special unit requiring a specially trained and competent commander because all the ships from all these command sectors had arrived there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Those were not special boats. Those were the slowest boats and the smallest possible combat unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Petre Handzijev the chief of the operations centre in Kumbor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. But that operations centre was never really operational because Kumbor is not where command was exercised, but rather it was from Kupari. Kumbor was only used for evacuation for the navy, the logistics for the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not go any further into that. Can you please tell us if Petre Handzijev was promoted to the rank of warship, battleship captain which would roughly be consistent with the rank of colonel in the ground forces?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure when and if that happened, certainly not while I was there. It would not have been possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Frigate Captain Jovo Drljan, was he assigned tasks as a capable and experienced officer at sea, something to do with ships?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: He left ship on account of his illness, and he never came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a document distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Frigate Captain Jovan Drljan also had a child who was ill?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know that. Seriously ill, in fact. And he was transferred to Boka on account of that, I believe, from Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1991, did Milan Zec become chief of staff and Slobodan Kozaric chief of the operations and training organ at the command of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please have a look at this document. Is that document an order to Frigate Captain Jovo Drljan to relocate three patrol boats from the Pula sector? Is this a combat order of the commander of the 9th VPS, Krsto Djurovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This document precedes the time of Admiral Jokic's assumption of his duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How is this relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the only relevance is the assessment of the officers' ability and the statement that this witness had left ship and no longer carried out any tasks at sea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be allowed to explain, I will only be too glad to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the sake of time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have one minute, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this document please be marked as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll leave that for the moment. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, you mentioned that in December, General Strugar, General Zivota Panic and yourself were at the positions of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. So in December 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please have the following document distributed. This is a document of which I have no translation. It is a document that we obtained from the OTP seven days ago. Mr. Jokic, what was General Zivota Panic's position in December 1991? Do you know which position he held?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: He was the deputy chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he was back in March 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: He was deputy chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document where it says, "The second box, Gornji Brgat, 25th of March 1992, Wednesday." Can you please read what the first passage says.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: This is no kind of document at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the war diary of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, if I may remind you. This is an excerpt, page 47, this document was given to us by the OTP. If you can please just read the first passage.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: "The unit was visited by Admiral Jokic, Lieutenant General Panic and Strugar between 9.45 and 10.50. They were at Zarkovica where they inspected the front positions of our units." But this is not true at all. It has nothing whatsoever to do with what really happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is my submission to you, Mr. Jokic, that you made the very same entry in your combat report that you made on the 25th of March 1992. You are the author of that combat report to the command of the 2nd Operational Group where this is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: General Panic was sent by General Kadijevic after the 6th of December to see what had happened. Later on, there was no unit in that position. Therefore, this has nothing to do with what really was the case. This is completely untruthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may this Defence exhibit please be marked. May this document please be marked as Defence exhibit. Your Honour, if I may, just two further questions, brief ones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, you've run out of time. We are over time by five minutes already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May we just have these documents admitted as Defence exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Holding over for the moment, two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now you've got a couple minutes. One question, Mr. Rodic. One more question, Mr. Rodic. Make your choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 5th of December following negotiations in Cavtat, you went to Kumbor along with your chief of staff and the assistant for ground forces, and you left the forward command post without its commander and without the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your excuse, the pretext so that you can say that the attack on Srdj on the 6th of December was an independent decision made by Vladimir Kovacevic because you had ordered an attack that not even your superior command or the military leadership in Belgrade knew about.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC
utterances.text: No, there's not even a grain of truth to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, any submissions with respect to this document that's being put as an extract of the war diary?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This document, the so-called war diary has been rejected by the witness. And he has denied it. We would object, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To the document which you provided to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This war diary has been rejected by the -- we vouch for nothing in it, Your Honours. If it's given to us, we pass on whatever's there. We would strongly object to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The record reveals its content, Mr. Rodic, and the admiral's position with respect to it. You had him read the material passage, so I think it is unnecessary for our evaluation of it and its effect on our evidence, it's unnecessary for the document itself to be admitted. What you would want to get from it is already in the record. We see no sufficient relevance of the other document to the matters that were the subject of this further evidence from the admiral, so it won't be admitted. So neither document will be admitted. Thank you very much, Admiral, for the time that you have been with us again this further time. There is time now for you to collect your thoughts and speak to your counsel before going to your Pre-Trial Conference. We once again -- yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting you. However, I wish to inform the Chamber that following today's testimony by this witness, pursuant to Rule 85(A)(iv), the Defence will be proposing certain exhibits to the Trial Chamber. There's a deadline that needs to be set, and may it at least be two weeks. We shall inform the Chamber in writing as well as our learned friends and colleagues what the evidence would be on the part of the Defence team pursuant to Rule 85(A)(iv).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Any proposal will be put forward in writing and that must be done within fourteen days of today, that is, it must be within a fortnight of today, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Prosecution will have a further week to respond. And we will then determine whether or not any or all of those documents should be received. That concludes the evidence, subject to the outstanding matters that were identified yesterday and this further matter just raised by Mr. Petrovic today. That concludes the evidence. We will now adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.
